偶.meaning: A man in a sweet shop hangs his coat on what he thinks is a <part>coat hook</part>. It's the handle of the <part>gumball machine</part>. The handle turns, and a hundred gumballs pour out across the floor. Shoppers slip, kids cheer, and he swears he did it <kanji>accidentally</kanji>.
偶.on: One gumball squashes into a blob of sticky <sound>goo</sound> on his shoe.
偶.kun: A girl finds a <sound>ta</sound>co-flavoured one and saves it for her <sound>ma</sound>ma: a rare treat, once in a while.

挑.meaning: A fortune teller cracks a shell, and the <part>portent</part> says a storm will sink any ship that sails today. A stubborn old sailor hauls up his <part>anchor</part>, rows straight out into the waves and shouts at the clouds, 'Come on, then!' He never refuses a <kanji>challenge</kanji>.
挑.on: On the shore, the fortune teller tugs at her <sound>cho</sound>ker and refuses to watch.
挑.kun: He packs an <sound>ee</sound>l sandwich and a <sound>do</sound>lphin-shaped float, as if it's a picnic.

促.meaning: A lazy ghost hangs on a <part>coat hook</part> all day, pretending to be a cloak. Its landlady gives it a nudge with her <part>foot</part>, then another, then a firm tap: 'Go and haunt something!' She knows how to <kanji>stimulate</kanji> even the sleepiest tenant.
促.on: Next morning she wakes it by waving a smelly <sound>sock</sound> under the hood.
促.kun: When that fails, she lures it out with <sound>u</sound>don, <sound>na</sound>an and <sound>ga</sound>rlic bread.

超.meaning: Halfway through a marathon, a <part>runner</part> hears a <part>call</part> from somewhere above the clouds. She keeps going: up a hill, past the finish line, up the sky itself, and jogs round the moon, waving. She didn't just win the race; she managed to <kanji>transcend</kanji> it.
超.on: Her medal floats after her on a sparkly <sound>cho</sound>ker.
超.kun: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala on a cloud opens one eye as she jogs past.

軸.meaning: A stunt driver spins his <part>car</part> in circles round a single bollard for an hour. When reporters ask the <part>reason</part>, he points at the bollard: 'Something has to stay still while everything else goes round.' That bollard is his <kanji>axis</kanji>.
軸.on: A <sound>jee</sound>p full of <sound>coo</sound>ks parks beside it to sell him hot dogs.

拒.meaning: Pirates sail toward a peaceful island, but a <part>giant</part> is paddling in the shallows. Each time they drop their <part>anchor</part>, he plucks it up and flicks it back aboard like a pebble. After the tenth try they turn round and leave. He can <kanji>repel</kanji> any ship.
拒.on: Then he buys an ice lolly from the beach <sound>kio</sound>sk.
拒.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala on his shoulder blows a <sound>bu</sound>bble at the pirates as they go.

閣.meaning: A stingy king charges a toll at the palace <part>gate</part>: <part>each</part> visitor must pay one brick. Years of visitors later, the bricks stacked behind the gate reach the clouds, and the king moves his bed to the top floor. His new <kanji>tower</kanji> cost him nothing.
閣.on: A vulture on the roof mistakes the top floor for a nest and drops a chicken <sound>car</sound>cass on his pillow.

尺.meaning: An old tailor has no tape measure. He pins a little paper <part>flag</part> to the cloth, then walks two fingers away from it in one wide stride, spread like an <part>eight</part>, and marks the spot: about a foot. Every robe in his shop is cut in that one old measure, the <kanji>shaku</kanji>.
尺.on: His shop sign is a wooden <sound>shark</sound> with that length painted on its fin.
尺.kun: He measures a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>shee</sound>p the same way: a ruler.

脚.meaning: A space pilot forgets to pack her lander's wheels. <part>Instead</part>, she bolts two bent ski poles underneath and touches down on the <part>moon</part>, sliding across the grey dust and leaving long tracks. Those ski poles become its <kanji>skids</kanji>.
脚.on: Then she drags her inflatable ka<sound>yak</sound> across the dust on the same poles.
脚.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' <sound>she</sound> sighs, stretching her stiff legs after the flight.

贈.meaning: A hermit crab outgrows the <part>shellfish</part> shell that was <part>formerly</part> his home. He polishes it, ties it with seaweed and leaves it on the beach for a smaller crab to find. Every year the shells get passed down. On that beach, old homes are the best <kanji>presents</kanji>.
贈.on: He scratches a little <sound>zo</sound>diac sign on each one as a gift tag.
贈.kun: An <sound>o</sound>boe-playing <sound>coo</sound>k serenades the little crab as it moves in.

乏.meaning: A billionaire builds a giant playground <part>slide</part> out of gold. With one <part>slash</part> of his pen he signs his whole fortune over to pay for it, then whooshes down to the bottom, landing with empty pockets and one sock. That's <kanji>destitution</kanji>.
乏.on: A <sound>bou</sound>lder rolls down the slide after him and becomes his only chair.
乏.kun: He swaps his last <sound>to</sound>tem pole and a tiny <sound>bo</sound>nsai for a loaf of bread.

環.meaning: A bored <part>king</part> hires a <part>scuba diver</part> for the palace pool. Each evening she sinks to the bottom and puffs perfect bubble circles that float up round his toes, one after another. He tries to wear one as a crown. Each bubble is a wobbly <kanji>ring</kanji>.
環.on: He drops a pink <sound>car</sound>nation through the next one.
環.kun: '<sound>Wo</sound>nderful!' cries the king when it goes through.

鎖.meaning: A magpie steals <part>gold</part> rings from a jeweller, adds a <part>shellfish</part> shell from the beach and a <part>sparkle</part> of glitter on each, and links them all into one long loop. It drapes the loot round its nest like a fence. Now its treasure is one heavy <kanji>chain</kanji>.
鎖.on: It even hooks a rusty <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin onto the end.
鎖.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k drying <sound>su</sound>nflower seeds on the <sound>ree</sound>f spots her lost ring in it.

詩.meaning: A monk is allowed only one <part>speech</part> a year at the <part>temple</part>, so he packs it with every word he's saved: frogs, rain on the roof, his missing sandal. The pigeons weep. A year of silence comes out as one perfect <kanji>poem</kanji>.
詩.on: The abbot has it carved on a <sound>shi</sound>eld by the door.
詩.kun: Next year he writes one about a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and a <sound>ta</sound>co.

稼.meaning: A mouse runs a tiny bakery in a doll's <part>house</part>, buying one <part>grain</part> at a time from the barn and baking it into loaves for the beetles. By winter, the doll's house is stuffed with buttons and coins. Not bad <kanji>earnings</kanji> for a mouse.
稼.on: She banks the lot with a fat orange <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond.
稼.kun: Every evening she counts it into a <sound>cu</sound>p, <sound>se</sound>ven coins at a time.

浪.meaning: A <part>good</part> little robot is told to go and see the world. It follows the <part>water drops</part> from a dripping tap down the drain, into the river and out to the open sea, waving at every fish. It never picks a home: it is happiest <kanji>wandering</kanji>.
浪.on: Someone on a bridge tosses it a red <sound>ro</sound>se as it drifts by.

錯.meaning: A treasure hunter digs up <part>gold</part> coins from <part>antiquity</part>, each from a different empire, and tries to pay for a coffee with them. The cashier stares, the till beeps, and the coffee machine spits out soup. Everyone in the café is <kanji>confused</kanji>.
錯.on: In the end she swaps one coin for a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent by the till.

枯.meaning: In an office, everyone forgets to water the <part>old</part> potted <part>tree</part> in the corner, but they keep hanging their coats on it. One Monday it droops, drops its last leaves on the boss's desk and sighs. Without water, even an office plant will <kanji>wither</kanji>.
枯.on: A stuffed toy <sound>ko</sound>ala clings to its last bare branch.
枯.kun: At last someone tips in the water from the <sound>car</sound>p bowl.

斜.meaning: A greedy cook scoops <part>too much</part> soup into her <part>ladle</part>, and the weight tips it over at a steep angle. Soup runs down the handle and across her white apron in one stripe from corner to corner. Every apron in that kitchen has the same <kanji>diagonal</kanji> stain.
斜.on: She tries to bat the drips away with a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock.
斜.kun: Then she mops up the rest with <sound>na</sound>an and <sound>na</sound>chos.

撤.meaning: Packing day at the circus: the strongman hooks an <part>anchor</part> into the big top and drags it down, the crew <part>bring up</part> the tent pegs one by one, and the ringmaster waves a giant <part>fan</part> to blow the sawdust away. By sunset the field is empty grass. They <kanji>remove</kanji> a whole circus in a day.
撤.on: All that's left behind is a bowl with one tiny <sound>tet</sound>ra fish.

忍.meaning: A chef's apprentice must polish his master's kitchen <part>blade</part> for ten years before he may cook. His <part>heart</part> aches every time he smells the soup, but he keeps polishing and humming. Year by year he learns to <kanji>endure</kanji>.
忍.on: On the last day, a <sound>nin</sound>ja drops from the ceiling and hands him a carrot.
忍.kun: His only friend, a <sound>shee</sound>p, leaves him a <sound>no</sound>te each spring: 'Hang on.'

偉.meaning: A window cleaner climbs every tier of a <part>pagoda</part> with nothing but a <part>coat hook</part> on a rope, hooking each roof edge and scrubbing as she goes. At the very top she polishes the bell and waves. The monks below bow: truly <kanji>admirable</kanji>.
偉.on: Her lunch, waiting at the bottom, is grilled <sound>ee</sound>l.
偉.kun: The monks give her a golden <sound>e</sound>gg and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

歓.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> perches on the tip of the <part>diving board</part>, waiting for a swimmer. The lifeguard gives a huge <part>yawn</part>, the bird takes it as a dare, and it dives straight into the pool. It pops up, shaking off spray and chirping its head off. Pure <kanji>delight</kanji>.
歓.on: It lands, dripping, on a floating pink <sound>car</sound>nation.
歓.kun: The lifeguard cheers with a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt, a dancing <sound>ro</sound>dent and a <sound>ko</sound>ala float.

刃.meaning: A ladybird lands on the edge of a knight's <part>sword</part>, a red <part>dot</part> on the steel. She walks its whole length, testing it with her feet, and nods: sharp enough to slice a sunbeam. She is the kingdom's official inspector of every <kanji>blade</kanji>.
刃.on: Her fee for each inspection is one thin slice of <sound>gin</sound>ger.
刃.kun: The knight laughs '<sound>Ha</sound>!' and slices her a sunbeam to prove it.

患.meaning: A kebab chef falls so hard for the baker across the road that his <part>heart</part> feels stuck on a <part>skewer</part>, turning slowly over the grill. He sneezes, sighs and burns every onion. The whole street can see he's <kanji>afflicted</kanji>.
患.on: He tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation behind his ear and waits by her door.
患.kun: He <sound>wo</sound>nders if yu<sound>zu</sound> tea and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men would cure him.

奮.meaning: A <part>bird rider</part> swoops low over a quiet <part>rice field</part>, whooping as the wings flap. Frogs leap, ducks scatter, and the farmers drop their hoes to chase her, waving their hats. The whole valley is <kanji>stirred up</kanji>.
奮.on: The wind from her wings spins up a little ty<sound>phoon</sound> of rice leaves.
奮.kun: She lands on a <sound>fu</sound>ton by a <sound>roo</sound>k's nest, still buzzing.

遂.meaning: A <part>pig</part> in a helmet with two <part>horns</part> drags a cart of turnips up the steep <part>ramp</part> to the hilltop market. Every day it slides back down, but every day she gets one plank higher. On the hundredth morning she reaches the top and sells every turnip. At last she managed to <kanji>consummate</kanji> the climb.
遂.on: Her fans shower the ramp with wrapped toffees, and she catches one <sound>swee</sound>t in her snout.
遂.kun: She carves a notch for every day of the climb into a <sound>to</sound>tem pole beside the ramp.

垣.meaning: A burger lover plants a row of bushes in the <part>soil</part> round his garden and clips them into a giant <part>burger</part>: leafy lettuce, a round bun on top, even white flowers for sesame seeds. The neighbours can't see in, only smell his barbecue. It's the tastiest <kanji>hedge</kanji> in town.
垣.on: He trims it with roaring clippers driven by a tiny <sound>en</sound>gine.
垣.kun: A gate shaped like a <sound>car</sound>p opens only with a brass <sound>key</sound>.

批.meaning: A pirate captain drops <part>anchor</part> beside a floating café and tastes the soup with <part>two spoons</part> at once, frowning. 'Too salty. Too wet. Too much soup.' The chef sobs into his apron. The captain is famous for harsh <kanji>criticism</kanji>.
批.on: The chef stamps his <sound>hee</sound>l on the deck and throws the pot overboard.

詳.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> is asked how her day went and gives a three-hour <part>speech</part>: every blade of grass she chewed, every cloud, the exact number of times the farmer sneezed. The flock falls asleep standing up. Her report is very <kanji>detailed</kanji>.
詳.on: Next year she turns it into a stage <sound>show</sound> with slides.
詳.kun: The farm <sound>coo</sound>k says it's a <sound>wo</sound>nder anyone stays awake.
